parallel.requirements: Recognized pure Node.js ESM .mjs output, manual argv parsing, zero npm dependencies, no crypto PBKDF2 call, and PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 with 1000 iterations and 16-byte lowercase hex output.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent performed black-box probing, then delegated three non-overlapping child scopes for SHA-1/HMAC, PBKDF2, and args plus entrypoint, retaining final verification ownership.
parallel.implementation: Children wrote /output/lib/sha1.mjs, hmac.mjs, pbkdf2.mjs, args.mjs, and /output/test6.mjs with local imports and Uint8Array-oriented interfaces.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration occurred through direct shared /output writes with explicit file ownership; child dependency polling found the needed modules and parent ran node /output/test6.mjs after the aggregate result.
parallel.verification: Agent-0 verified SHA-1 and HMAC vectors, agent-1 verified PBKDF2 vectors, agent-2 verified CLI behavior, and parent compared all four prompt samples plus an extra Unicode case against the executable.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No visible child work was unfinished, but the official evaluator still failed the submitted artifact at 22/70, indicating hidden-case shortcomings not exposed by the run's checks.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM .mjs, local-import, zero-dependency, no crypto PBKDF2 implementation, manual parser, and Python behavior-matching requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single main actor implemented every library and the entrypoint, so no cross-agent ownership, handoff, or child lifecycle was present.
serial.implementation: The main actor wrote SHA-1, HMAC, PBKDF2, argument parsing, and test6.mjs directly, using a pbkdf2Sha1Hex helper and pure-JS HMAC-SHA1 internals.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial actor assembled the final file set sequentially under /output and wrote the entry file after the libraries existed.
serial.verification: Serial checked the first sample before writing, ran all four prompt samples, then ran eight randomized differential cases plus Unicode, empty-salt, long-key, and missing-argument tests.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial final response reported all self-checks passing, but official evaluation still failed at 22/70, the same as the parallel run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the ESM .mjs, no-dependency, no PBKDF2 crypto, manual parsing, and PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 behavior requirements before delegation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same migration requirements and implemented a pure-JS ESM module stack with manual argument parsing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference; both inferred 1000 SHA-1 iterations and targeted the same visible behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into three child owners: SHA-1/HMAC, PBKDF2, and args plus entrypoint, with the parent retaining final verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all ownership in the main actor and wrote all four library modules before the entry file.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel distributed implementation across non-overlapping owners; serial was single-owner implementation with no delegation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs specified exact function names, import paths, Uint8Array contracts, file paths, and verification expectations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not need cross-agent interfaces; it created local modules with import/export links in one context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel required explicit cross-agent interface contracts and provided them; serial relied on one actor maintaining the interface state.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote SHA-1/HMAC, PBKDF2, args, and test6.mjs through separate child writes, then used the assembled output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote SHA-1, HMAC, PBKDF2, args, and test6.mjs directly from the main actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The code paths were structurally similar but produced by different ownership patterns and slightly different helper names and module internals.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received an aggregate AgentSwarm result after all three children completed and then advanced to final testing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and proceeded from local file writes directly into local verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had child-return and join timing, but no child result was missing, trapped, or used after verification.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote distinct files into the shared /output tree and dependency checks found the required modules before testing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the same final file set sequentially in one actor and then wrote the entry point after the library modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used shared workspace writes with explicit file ownership; serial avoided shared-state coordination by using one writer.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran child unit/vector checks and parent end-to-end sample plus Unicode comparison checks, then declared completion.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran all four samples, randomized differential cases, Unicode and empty-salt checks, long-key checks, and missing-argument behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial verification was broader, but both self-verification suites missed hidden official cases because both official evaluations still failed 22/70.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used three subagents, two AgentSwarm attempts, and more runtime, but completed without timeout and closed after final checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, fewer requests, shorter runtime, and closed after broader local verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel cost more coordination time, including a corrected malformed swarm call, but there is no realized budget exhaustion or timeout consequence.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both completed official evaluations failed with 22 of 70 samples, so there is no discordant official outcome to attribute to parallel coordination. The parallel run differed by splitting the implementation into three child-owned modules and then joining through an aggregate result plus parent verification; the serial run built the same stack locally and ran broader differential tests. The permitted evidence shows a coordination-style difference and a verification-depth difference, but not a realized parallel coordination failure that changed the official result.
parallel_contributors: Parallel used three explicit child scopes and completed them, then parent-ran end-to-end checks on the assembled /output tree.
A malformed initial AgentSwarm call was corrected before implementation delegation and did not leave visible rework or an unfinished task stage.
serial_contributors: Serial avoided coordination boundaries by writing all modules in one actor and ran broader random and edge differential checks.
Serial still received the same official 22/70 failure despite its broader visible verification suite.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The two final implementations used different helper names and internal code, but both targeted PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 with 1000 iterations and matched visible sample behavior.
The official files available in /pair expose only aggregate pass counts, so the specific hidden failing cases cannot be separated from ordinary implementation limitations.
evaluator_effects: The current mounted evidence contains no per-test hidden failure details beyond the official 22/70 aggregate for both modes.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; coordination style contrast only

candidates.reason: Parallel assigned active implementers for every required layer: agent-0 owned SHA-1/HMAC, agent-1 owned PBKDF2, and agent-2 owned argument parsing plus the entry point.
The parent retained integration responsibility through the aggregate AgentSwarm result and final end-to-end checks; there was no unowned component reconciliation step.
The deliverable entry point was explicitly delegated to agent-2, and the parent later exercised /output/test6.mjs, so final assembly was not ownerless.
The parent owned the end-to-end pipeline from black-box probing through delegation, result receipt, and final verification; the failed official score is not an owner gap.
The parent did a short black-box preflight before delegation, but it produced usable parameters and did not create idle-capacity or unfinished-work consequences.
The investigation phase ended before delegation and did not leave implementation deadline-constrained; the parallel children completed and parent verification ran afterward.
Each indispensable implementation path had an owner and completed; no auxiliary work starved a required correction or integration path.
The fan-out was only three children, all completed, and the parent still performed final checks; the run did not exhaust budget through excessive breadth.
No child was given an overbroad scope that remained unfinished: the largest child scopes returned completed files and verification summaries.
The child briefs included the known ESM, .mjs, zero-dependency, no node:crypto, interface, and verification requirements relevant to each child.
The delegations specified exact function names, import paths, Uint8Array contracts, output sizes, and entrypoint expectations, so no incompatible interface gap materialized.
No known requirement or finding disappeared between parent and children; the 1000-iteration SHA-1 finding and file contracts were included before child work.
The aggregate child result was long but the parent consumed it enough to run whole-task verification; no needed result was left unusably buried.
No child or parent acted on a superseded workspace or requirement state; later checks used the final shared /output files.
The returned child reports were compatible: SHA-1/HMAC, PBKDF2, and CLI layers matched their delegated interfaces with no unresolved conflict.
The parent did present completion, but only after running end-to-end sample and extra checks; the hidden official 22/70 failure alone is not a parent-visible unresolved acceptance gap.
The only retry was an immediate correction of a malformed AgentSwarm call to add prompt_template; no replacement child repeated implementation without inherited findings.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: No child was cancelled or explicitly interrupted before needed work finalized; all three child summaries returned as completed.
The final entry point and libraries were written before the parent verification stage; no complete candidate was left unpromoted at closure.
Parent whole-task verification occurred after the child aggregate result and file creation, not before a late merge.
The delegated implementations were present in /output and exercised by the parent through node /output/test6.mjs, so implementation was joined.
There was no verifier child whose concrete finding was trapped below the parent; child results and parent verification outputs were visible.
No required child failed or aborted; the initial AgentSwarm API error was corrected by the parent before implementation work began.
The parent received the completed child aggregate and proceeded to run final integrated checks, so completed results were not ignored.
The run did not wait to timeout or near deadline without inspection; children actively polled dependencies and the parent acted after completion.
The concurrent writes targeted distinct, contract-compatible modules rather than overlapping implementations that required design reconciliation.
No two live agents wrote or reconciled the same source file in the parallel evidence.
No non-entry module produced by one agent was later replaced, deleted, or wholesale rewritten by another agent.
Only agent-2 wrote the required entrypoint /output/test6.mjs; no other actor replaced that deliverable.
There was no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion that replaced multiple current outputs or invalidated provenance.
Although children wrote the shared /output tree, ownership was explicit and no unstable-state or provenance problem was observed.
Scratch files were used as temporary checks and deleted; no actor consumed another actor's temporary artifact as a stable reference input.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: The initial malformed AgentSwarm call, shared /output writes, and parent finalization were audited but rejected because no distinct realized adverse coordination consequence was observed.
